text:
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): Hey team — during onboarding our Node SDK started returning 403 for some requests after ~2m, then a flurry of 429s. Logs show 'invalid_token' followed immediately by 'quota_exceeded: per_key'. Any idea what's up?
Priya Khatri: Thanks Jorge. Which SDK + version and are you using our edge proxy or calling the API directly?
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): node-sdk v2.1.0, calling through our edge reverse-proxy. We do short-lived tokens (TTL 120s). We refresh tokens proactively at ~30s before expiry.
Alex Chen: Can you paste the SDK config you pass for refresh/grace? small snippet is fine.
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): Sure — here's the relevant part from their init: ```json
{
  "api_key": "REDACTED",
  "token_ttl": 120,
  "refresh_before_sec": 30,
  "key_grace_seconds": 60
}
```
Samir Patel: Hmm — that key_grace_seconds value stands out. Is that an internal param on their side or something our SDK surface exposes?
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): It's a local param in their auth helper — they hold the old token for 60s while swapping. Thought it was safer to avoid gaps.
Priya Khatri: That could explain it. If their proxy / client keeps sending the old token while trying the new one, our rate limiter may see two rapid auth attempts with different session IDs and count both against the per-key quota.
Alex Chen: Can you share a short curl trace of a failing request? Something like: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <tokenA>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
# then immediately with tokenB```
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): Pasted from their debug run: ```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
# 85s later (still same conn)
HTTP/1.1 403 {"error":"invalid_token","detail":"token_revoked"}
HTTP/1.1 429 {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota":"per_key"}
```
Samir Patel: Two quick notes: 1) the 403 suggests our introspection rejects that token (revoked/expired) — but the 429 right after suggests the client retried aggressively, which pushed them over per-key rate rules. 2) If the proxy queues old token headers while the backend accepts the new one, you get duplicate auth attempts in a short window.
Priya Khatri: Proposed next steps: 1) ask customer to set key_grace_seconds to <=5s for a test run, 2) we can enable a temporary relaxed per-key window for Acme to avoid throttling while we validate, 3) eng to review our token revocation logs for their key around 1766004200-1766004400.
Alex Chen: I'll take the eng action. @CS Bot can you open an internal ticket and attach the logs Jorge just pasted? label: onboarding, auth, rate-quota.
CS Bot: Ticket created: #CS-7892 — attachments: paste from Jorge, initial hypothesis (grace window + proxy queuing).
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): I can try the <=5s test now and report back in ~10m. Thanks y'all. :pray:
Samir Patel: Meanwhile I'll grep for their key in revocation logs and check if there was a TTL mismatch or an accidental server-side revoke. Will update thread once I have findings.
Priya Khatri: Good plan. If the small-grace test clears it, we should update our onboarding doc to call out proxy header buffering and recommend a short swap window, plus a troubleshooting checklist for 403->429 cascades.
Alex Chen: Agree. Also adding a CLI snippet we can share with customers to reproduce safely: ```bash
# generate tokenA, wait 95s, generate tokenB, fire both quickly to reproduce
node reproduce-auth-swap.js --ttl 120 --refresh-delay 30 --parallel 2
```
Jorge Alvarez (Acme): Ran the small-grace test — looks promising, single 200 returned and no 429s for the next 5m. Will keep monitoring during our traffic ramp.
Samir Patel: I pulled logs — no server-side revoke during the window, just many overlapping auth checks from the same key. Confirms client-side buffering hypothesis.
Priya Khatri: Great closure. Action items: Jorge to continue ramp and confirm, Alex to update playbook with header-buffer note + sample reproduce script, Samir to close CS-7892 with eng notes. Thanks everyone. :tada:
